stories.summary: At COP31, Sustainability and Environment Minister Grace Fu said Singapore will review its decarbonisation plans across all sectors and take stock of progress under the Green Plan 2030, as geopolitical tensions and inflation slow global climate action. She signalled the carbon tax could sit at the lower end of the S$50–80 per tonne range by 2030 if momentum keeps fading.
stories.title: Singapore to review decarbonisation plans as global climate action slows
stories.why: A signal that Singapore may recalibrate its climate targets — including the carbon tax — to the pace of global action.

stories.summary: The Straits Times profiles four hawkers in their 80s — including an 88-year-old in Toa Payoh and an 86-year-old roasting about 80kg of pork daily in People's Park Food Centre — who keep working long hours because retirement feels boring and lonely, not for lack of family support.
stories.title: No time to retire: Why these Singapore hawkers are grinding on in their 80s
stories.why: A window on Singapore's ageing hawker workforce — and why the trade's succession problem runs deeper than money.

stories.summary: Reuters reported the SEC is examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia, sending shares down about 14% on Friday and erasing roughly $500 billion in market value in a single day. Scrutiny includes how Nvidia reports revenue by geography — about $104 billion was booked through its Singapore unit in 2025 — and $118 billion in customer guarantees.
stories.title: Nvidia Stock Plunge Wipes Out Nearly $500 Billion in One Day as SEC Reportedly Probes Its Accounting
stories.why: The world's most important AI company now faces a regulator probe with a direct Singapore angle, on top of its CEO crisis.

stories.summary: President Trump said the US wants only older-generation chips sold to China — 'we don't mind if none go. But only older' — and that his administration is discussing a comprehensive agreement with Beijing, without giving details.
stories.title: Trump says only older chips should be sold to China
stories.why: Draws the line for US chip exports to China after a week of tighter curbs, with direct consequences for the region's chip trade.

stories.summary: President Trump called on Nvidia to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang, saying he should make 'a big apology and go back', and said he discussed Huang with Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Nvidia's board has said it does not intend to reinstate Huang.
stories.title: Trump calls for Nvidia's Huang to be given 'second chance'
stories.why: The president is publicly pressing Nvidia's board on its most consequential decision since Huang's resignation.

stories.summary: President Trump said US tech companies would face 'a tremendous tax' if they build AI data centers abroad, but gave no details and said he had not yet told his own officials about the plan. He also urged Americans to welcome data-center construction at home and extract concessions from developers.
stories.title: Trump says he plans to penalize companies that build data centers in other countries
stories.why: A new threat to the AI buildout's global footprint, floated without a plan behind it.

stories.summary: A string of outages hitting Microsoft email, the FAA, major banks and the NSA's internal systems has raised questions about US cybersecurity, though officials say they were not attacks. Former CISA director Chris Krebs blamed rushed patches for bugs being found rapidly with AI, and Trump has replaced national cyber director Sean Cairncross with Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies.
stories.title: Mounting tech disruptions raise concerns about U.S. cybersecurity
stories.why: The week's outages show how AI is accelerating both the discovery of software flaws and the pressure to patch them.

stories.summary: US stocks extended their rout on Friday: the Dow fell 949.73 points (1.93%) to 48,147.33, the S&P 500 lost 3.70% to 6,910.42 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.28% to 22,617.73. The S&P and Dow are now more than 10% below their record highs — a correction — and the S&P has fallen seven straight sessions, its longest streak since February 2020.
stories.title: US stocks end sharply lower on AI selloff; S&P 500, Dow in correction
stories.why: The AI trade that powered markets for two years is now in a full correction, with the week's losses the worst since April 2025.

stories.summary: Spot gold fell to about $3,537.90 an ounce, down 2.38%, after touching $3,502.93, its lowest since September 2025; silver slid 3.83% to about $41.12. Gold is down 9.5% and silver 16% for the week as expectations of further Fed rate rises and a strong dollar punish precious metals.
stories.title: Gold falls toward $3,500, silver slides as stock markets enter correction territory
stories.why: The metals rout is the other side of the hawkish-Fed trade — and silver's weekly collapse dwarfs gold's.

stories.summary: Bitcoin slumped as much as 6.1% to $57,716 — its lowest in more than two years — as the global market rout dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin has now shed more than 20% of its value in November.
stories.title: Bitcoin Falls to More than Two-Year Low as Global Markets Sink
stories.why: The crypto sell-off is deepening alongside the AI stock rout, with record ETF outflows adding to the pressure.

stories.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook made the case for more rate rises, saying the policy rate is 'not high enough' to deal with inflation she views with 'great concern' and that waiting risks falling behind the curve. Markets broadly expect the Fed to raise rates at its December 8–9 meeting.
stories.title: Fed's Cook says rate hikes needed to lower high inflation
stories.why: The hawkish Fed message is the thread behind this week's equity and metals sell-off.

stories.summary: Russia launched one of its largest air attacks of the war hours after Putin's talks with Trump and Xi in Shenzhen: more than 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic, and 400-plus drones. At least eight people were killed, three bridges across the Dnipro in Kyiv were damaged, and two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in Poland near a Coalition of the Willing exercise.
stories.title: Ukraine Reports Russian Missile Blitz After Putin Met With Trump
stories.why: Putin's promised 'far more painful' retaliation for the Crimea bridge strikes arrived within hours of the peace summit — and spilled into NATO territory.

stories.summary: Russian forces struck the centre of Kryvyi Rih with ballistic missiles on the evening of 20 November, killing a seven-year-old boy and a female paramedic who had arrived at the scene, and injuring at least 21 people, including three children.
stories.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on central Kryvyi Rih: child and paramedic killed, at least 21 injured
stories.why: A second deadly strike in a day shows the barrage is continuing into the weekend, not a one-night event.

stories.summary: King Mohammed VI allocated 4 billion dirhams (€366 million) from the Hassan II Fund for a defence-industry roadmap to 2035, aiming for 50,000 jobs, 40% of the armed forces' equipment needs met domestically, and over 65% of industry revenue from exports. Priority areas include drones, land and naval systems, defence electronics, cybersecurity and AI.
stories.title: Morocco commits €366 million to build a national defence industry by 2035
stories.why: Another state is moving to build a sovereign defence industrial base — with drones and AI on the priority list.

stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed six people in Gaza on Friday despite the ceasefire, the civil defense agency said; the military said it had targeted 'multiple military operatives'. The strikes came a day after the army completed a rare ground incursion in central Gaza, and more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began in October 2025.
stories.title: Gaza civil defense says Israeli strikes kill six
stories.why: The ceasefire keeps fraying — each side accuses the other of violations, and the death toll since October keeps climbing.

stories.summary: A UN conference in Geneva on lethal autonomous weapons ran past its Friday deadline into Saturday after Russia in particular slowed five days of talks among 128 countries. A majority favour a legally binding agreement, but the US and Russia are reluctant and full consensus is required; a draft proposes negotiations toward a 'framework protocol'.
stories.title: 'Killer robots' talks run into overtime
stories.why: The first global rules for weapons that can kill without human intervention are stuck on consensus — with the states that hold the technology least keen.

stories.summary: Gen. Sir Rob Magowan, head of the UK's Cyber & Specialist Operations Command, confirmed for the first time that the National Cyber Force carries out offensive cyber operations against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea. Asked if Britain is at cyber war with them, he said: 'I wouldn't say we're at war, but we're not at peace either.'
stories.title: UK confirms offensive cyber operations targeting Russia, China, Iran, North Korea
stories.why: A rare public admission that the UK is already conducting offensive cyber operations — in the 'grey zone' below open conflict.

stories.summary: Security experts warn AI founders and staff are prime honey-trap targets because the most valuable secrets now sit inside companies building chips and models. The warning follows allegations that Nvidia's Jensen Huang fell for a honey trap involving Alice Huang, a former executive of a Singapore neocloud accused of being a Chinese spy and smuggling restricted chips. OpenAI has warned employees about outsiders trying to befriend them for secrets, and AI has made such schemes cheaper to run.
stories.title: Experts warn: Nearly everyone in AI is susceptible to a honey-trap scheme right now
stories.why: The oldest espionage trick now targets the AI industry — and the Singapore neocloud at the centre of the Nvidia scandal is the case in point.

stories.summary: Bell Canada confirmed an 'agentic' threat actor breached its systems on 17 November and stole enterprise customer data, including from a pre-production system used to order and provision telecom circuits. Bell has not identified the attacker or said how many customers were affected; the stolen contact and ticket data could fuel targeted phishing and impersonation.
stories.title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
stories.why: A major carrier describing its attacker as 'agentic' is the clearest sign yet that AI-assisted intrusions have reached critical infrastructure.

tldr: Singapore: Singapore to review its decarbonisation plans as global climate action slows.
Technology: The SEC is probing Nvidia's accounting as its shares plunge 14%, wiping about $500bn.
Finance: Wall Street's rout deepens — the S&P 500 and Dow enter correction as the Nasdaq drops 5.28%.
Defence: Russia launches its biggest air assault of the year on Ukraine, and missiles stray into Poland.
Information warfare: The UK confirms offensive cyber operations against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea.
